calls.reason: Pairs c1000 (u only) with c1111 (all rules). u uses X-basis measurement instead of Toffolis to erase ANDs, so it should cut mean T without extra qubits. c1111 is the upper bound with every rule on. Comparing them against the c0000 parent shows u's effect and what r, free_s and combined_y add.

u alone cut T by ~3658 at fixed Q; adding r+free_s+combined_y (c1111) cut Q 214->198 (likely free_s) but added ~193 T. Testing c1110 (drop combined_y) and c1011 (drop r) keeps u+free_s and isolates which of r/combined_y causes the T overhead; either may beat c1111's QT by keeping Q=198 with lower T.

Archive deltas: free_s cuts Q 214→198 at about the same T. u cuts T by ~3.7k. r alone trims ~60 T (c1111 vs c1011). combined_y adds ~355 T (c1111 vs c1110). c1010 (u+free_s, no r) is the only unmeasured recipe likely near the c1110 frontier (est. QT ~5.55M), and it isolates whether r actually helps under free_s. c1100 (u+r, Q214) tests the r effect without free_s, separating the r and free_s interaction. All recipes without u are expected to sit near 31.6k T, which is dominated.

The archive shows rule u is the main lever on T: about 31.8k down to about 28.1k. free_s is the main lever on Q (214 down to 198). r gives a small T gain of about 60, and combined_y adds about 300 T. Every untested recipe without u should land near 31.7k T, so even with free_s its QT would be about 6.27M. The only two remaining recipes with u, c1101 and c1001, should come in around 214 x 28.3k, about 6.07M, so they have the lowest expected QT of what's left. They also test combined_y with u but without free_s, a combination not yet measured. Neither is likely to beat c1110 (5.53M), but this pair makes the best use of the last two slots.

c1111 enables all rules: u and r cut Toffolis spent on AND uncomputation and unread writes, combined_y merges coordinate products, and free_s lowers Q. It should give the lowest Q*T if the rules compose. c1101 is the same recipe without free_s, which is the one rule with a real trade-off (fewer qubits but extra Toffolis to rebuild the register). The pair measures whether free_s's qubit saving outweighs that cost, which guides the remaining slots.

c1111 is the best so far (QT 5,604,192). Going from c1101 to c1111 shows that free_s drops Q from 214 to 198 and leaves T almost unchanged. Nothing has yet shown which of u, r or combined_y produces the drop in T from 31,769 to about 28,300. Testing c1011 (r removed) and c1110 (combined_y removed) keeps u and free_s, which are known or likely to help. Each test removes one of the two rules whose effect is uncertain. If either rule adds Toffolis or scratch qubits through phase repair or a longer product expression, one of these recipes could match or beat c1111. If neither does, the results still show how much each rule contributes.

free_s is what lowers Q from 214 to 198, so the next tests should keep free_s on. The best result so far is c1110 (QT 5.53M). Comparing c1111 with c1011, adding r only cut T by about 61. Adding combined_y raised T a little (c1110 vs c1111). c1010 (u + free_s, no r) and c0110 (r + free_s, no u) are the two untested 198-qubit neighbours of the best recipe. Running both separates the effects of u and r. This tests whether r is really needed: c1010 could match or beat c1110. It also shows how much of the T reduction comes from u. Recipes without free_s stay at Q=214 and are unlikely to beat 5.53M.

From the archive: u cuts mean Toffolis by about 3.4k. free_s lowers Q from 214 to 198. combined_y adds about 355 Toffolis (c1111 vs c1110, c1011 vs c1010). r saves about 60. The best so far is c1110 (QT 5.53M). None of the remaining recipes combines u with free_s, so I expect none to beat it. The last two slots are better used to separate effects. c1100 tests u+r without free_s (estimate: Q 214, about 28.0k Toffolis, QT about 6.0M). c0010 tests free_s alone (Q 198), which isolates r's effect against c0110 without u.

With no slots used, the first test should be the full stack c1111. It uses u, r, free_s and combined_y together. u replaces AND erasure with X-basis measurement plus phase repair, which should cut executed Toffolis on uncompute. combined_y should cut the Toffolis spent on coordinate products. free_s should lower Q by releasing the cofactor register during inversion. r turns unread writes into phase operations. c0110 (r + free_s only) is a contrasting second recipe. It mainly tests whether the qubit-side rules lower Q alone. It also gives a fallback if u or combined_y fail the phase or scratch checks.

r/free_s (c0110) cut Q 214->198 with little T change; c1111 additionally adds u+combined_y and cuts T by ~3300, but the u vs combined_y contributions are confounded. c1110 (drop combined_y) and c0111 (drop u) are single-rule ablations of the best recipe that keep the Q reduction, isolating each T-reduction mechanism and possibly beating c1111 if one rule interacts negatively.

u cuts T by ~3.65k (c1110 vs c0110); combined_y adds T (+355/+576), so drop it. Every measured recipe has both r and free_s, so we can't tell which one brings Q from 214 to 198. c1100 (no free_s) and c1010 (no r) each differ from the best recipe, c1110, by one rule. Testing both shows which rule lowers Q. c1100 may also beat the best if reconstructing free_s costs Toffolis without saving qubits.

From the archive: free_s is what lowers Q (214→198). u gives the biggest T cut, about 3.7k (c0000→c1100). r saves only about 60 Toffolis (c1010 vs c1110). combined_y adds about 350–580 Toffolis (c1110→c1111, c0110→c0111). c1011 is the strongest untested recipe because it has both u and free_s. Its predicted QT is about 5.6M, close to the best so far (c1110, 5.53M), and running it tests whether combined_y behaves differently when r is off. c0010 adds free_s alone to the parent, which isolates that rule's effect on Q and T and fills a gap in the attribution. Recipes without free_s keep Q at 214, so they can't compete.

c1111 combines every Toffoli-reducing mechanism (u: measurement-based AND uncompute; r: unread writes to phase ops; combined_y: shared coordinate products) with free_s's qubit reduction, giving the largest expected Q*T drop. c1101 is the same recipe without free_s. Rebuilding the cofactor register adds Toffolis that could offset the qubit saving, so this pair directly measures whether free_s helps in Q*T terms.

free_s alone (c1101→c1111) cut Q 214→198 at about the same T, so it is kept. The ~11% T reduction from u, r and combined_y has not been split between them. c1110 drops combined_y and c0111 drops u (u overlaps with r, since both are phase-repair rewrites). These one-rule ablations around the best recipe c1111 show which T-saving rule is redundant, and either could beat c1111's QT if its dropped rule costs scratch qubits.

The archive shows free_s cuts Q from 214 to 198 (c1101 vs c1111), and u cuts T by about 3.9k (c0111 vs c1111). combined_y adds about 355 T (c1110 vs c1111). So the best candidate keeps u and free_s and drops combined_y. That leaves r: c1110 (r on) is the current best at QT 5.53M. c1010 tests whether dropping r does better still. c1011 pairs with c1111 to isolate r's effect when combined_y is on. Together they show whether r helps, and the batch includes the strongest untested candidate. Recipes without free_s (Q=214) or without u (high T) are unlikely to beat the frontier.

The archive shows clear patterns. Turning on free_s is what cuts qubits from 214 to 198. Turning on u is what cuts most of the Toffolis, about 3,800 fewer. combined_y adds about 355 Toffolis (c1111 vs c1110, and c1011 vs c1010), and r saves about 60. The current best is c1110 (QT 5,533,902). None of the remaining recipes has both u and free_s, so none is likely to beat it. With the last two slots, the most useful thing is to measure the two main effects on their own against the mfs parent: c1000 (u only) and c0010 (free_s only). That shows how much each rule contributes and whether u and free_s add up or interact in the measured frontier.

Pairs the full stack c1111 with the u+r core c1100. u and r cut Toffoli count by replacing AND uncomputation with measurement and phase fixups, which is where most of mean_T should drop. free_s should lower Q, and combined_y may cut product Toffolis further. Measuring the two together tells us whether free_s+combined_y add value on top of u+r, and if c1111 fails a check, c1100 is still a likely gain over the parent.

c1100 (u+r) cuts T from 31769 to 28051 and leaves Q at 214. c1111 brings Q down to 198 but pushes T up to 28304. So free_s and combined_y together save 16 qubits and cost about 250 Toffolis. Testing c1110 (u+r+free_s) and c1101 (u+r+combined_y) separates the two on the strong u+r base. Releasing the cofactor register most likely gives the Q saving. The combined expression or the reconstruction may be what adds T. Either recipe could keep Q near 198 with T near 28051, giving a QT around 5.55M, which would beat c1111's 5.60M.

The archive shows free_s cuts Q from 214 to 198 and also lowers T a little. combined_y adds Toffolis whether or not free_s is on (+355 with it, +342 without), so the best configuration should have free_s on and combined_y off. The current best is c1110 at QT 5.53M. Every measured recipe has u and r on together, so we don't yet know how much each one contributes to the roughly 3.7k drop in Toffolis. Testing c1010 (u alone) against c0110 (r alone), with the other settings at their best values, separates the two effects. If u and r overlap or r adds overhead, one of these could beat c1110.

From the archive: free_s cuts Q from 214 to 198 and T by ~100. u cuts T by ~3.7k (c0110 vs c1110). r changes T by ~60 or less. combined_y adds ~+350 to T (c1100→c1101, c1110→c1111). c1011 (u+free_s+y, Q198, predicted T ~28.36k, QT ~5.62M) has the best predicted QT of the unmeasured recipes and tests y without r, next to the frontier. c1000 (u alone, predicted QT ~6.0M) separates u's effect from r and free_s. It is the next-best candidate and checks additivity.
c1000 tests whether measurement-based AND erasure reduces Toffolis. c0010 tests whether releasing the cofactor reduces Q enough to offset reconstruction cost.

c1010 combines the measured Toffoli reduction from u with the measured qubit reduction from free_s. c1110 tests whether r further reduces their combined Q×T cost; these interactions remain unmeasured.
Both recipes test combined coordinate products while retaining the measured qubit savings from free_s and Toffoli savings from u. Their comparison isolates r, whose measured benefit was small.

c0110 and c1100 each remove one mechanism from the best measured recipe, c1110. They test whether AND erasure and cofactor release retain their benefits with phase conversion. Both avoid combined_y, which increased measured Toffolis in matched comparisons.

Both recipes use measurement-based AND erasure, unread-write conversion, and combined coordinate products. Their sole difference isolates whether cofactor release reduces Q enough to offset reconstruction Toffolis.
Both recipes retain measurement-based AND erasure and cofactor release. Each removes one rule from the best measured recipe, testing whether r or combined_y increases Q times mean Toffolis.
Both recipes release the cofactor register and omit combined_y, which raised mean Toffolis in the measured c1110/c1111 pair. Comparing c0110 with c1010 isolates the two phase-rewrite strategies.

Both recipes use measurement-based AND erasure, which shows the largest measured Toffoli reduction. They omit combined_y and test whether avoiding cofactor reconstruction offsets the higher qubit count; c1100 also tests phase conversion.
Both recipes use measurement erasure and phase operations to target fewer Toffolis. Their sole difference, free_s, tests whether qubit savings justify reconstruction cost.
c1111 tests combined coordinate products on the best measured recipe. c0010 isolates the qubit savings and reconstruction cost from free_s.
Test c0110 and c1010 to isolate phase conversion and measurement-based erasure against c1110. Both retain cofactor release and omit combined_y, which increased measured QT.

Both recipes use AND erasure, which shows the largest measured Toffoli reduction. c1011 also releases the cofactor register to reduce Q. c1101 tests combined coordinate products without cofactor reconstruction; their interaction remains unmeasured.
Both recipes use measurement-based erasure and phase operations to reduce Toffolis. Their sole difference, free_s, tests whether lower qubit use offsets reconstruction cost in Q times mean Toffolis.
c0111 and c1011 each remove one erasure rule from the best measured recipe. Both retain cofactor release and combined coordinate products, testing each rule's effect on Q times mean Toffolis.

Both recipes retain measurement-based AND erasure and cofactor release, which support lower T and Q. Comparing them tests phase conversion without combined_y and checks whether combined_y adds overhead.
Test whether removing cofactor reconstruction saves enough Toffolis to offset the larger register count. Comparing c1100 and c1000 also isolates phase conversion with AND erasure enabled.
c1000 tests whether measurement-based AND erasure lowers executed Toffolis. c1100 adds unread-write conversion, which isolates its extra effect on Q times mean Toffolis.

Both recipes extend the best measured parent, c1100. c1110 tests whether cofactor release reduces Q enough to offset reconstruction Toffolis. c1101 tests whether combined coordinate products reduce Toffolis.
c1010 retains AND erasure and cofactor release while testing the small measured benefit of r. c1111 tests whether cofactor release offsets the combined expression's measured Toffoli cost.
Both recipes release the cofactor register, which reduced Q in measured cases. Their comparison isolates the effect of phase rewrites without measurement erasure or combined coordinate products.
